title: introduce-helm-runtime-constraint-enforcer-and-staggered-bootstrap
author: Marcus Nguyen
description: Context: Private installs in large on-prem clusters often fail or cause noisy neighbor issues when operator defaults allow oversized pod requests or permissive affinity. This PR introduces a Helm-level constraint enforcement primitive and a staggered bootstrap sequence to reduce cluster pressure during tenant/namespace provisioning. Motivation: reduce failed init jobs on dense clusters, provide a declarative values contract for resource guardrails, and enable safer phased rollouts for Private deployments. What this PR does: adds a new top-level values block 'constraintPolicy' with templates for cpu/gpu/memory quotas, nodeAffinity profiles, and podTopologies; adds a lightweight init-controller Job template (charts/templates/init-constraint-assertion.yaml) that runs as a pre-seed gate to validate cluster capacity and optionally create a quota object; adds a 'bootstrapWave' parameter that lets Helm sequence tenant initialization across waves with per-wave delay and jitter (used by release engineers to stage mass upgrades); provides a 'prewarm.sidecar' optional container that runs image verification and pulls large base images in air-gapped installs before main init runs; introduces a 'canaryStrategy' templating helper to produce phased helm hooks for canary seed jobs; extends values.schema.json and README with examples and compatibility notes. Important safety behavior: by default the constraint enforcer operates in dry-run mode and emits events/logs only; operators must opt-in to 'enforce: true' to apply quota/affinity mutations. Rollback and upgrades: the bootstrapWave implementation is idempotent and records progress in a ConfigMap so interrupted upgrades resume without duplicating seed work. Compatibility: designed to be compatible with existing tenant-seed hooks and the private-installer's existing preflight probes. Testing: unit tests for templating helpers, end-to-end upgrade simulation in a small-kind cluster, and a staged upgrade run in our internal QA environment. Links: Linear tasks ENG-4123, ENG-4180. Checklist: - [x] values.schema updated - [x] templates added - [x] docs & examples - [x] dry-run default safety - [x] CI tests and e2e smoke

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Nice direction. Two asks: please make dry-run the default (so operators opt-in) and add clearer docs for how bootstrapWave interacts with helm --wait.
Author (Marcus Nguyen): Dry-run remains default; updated README with helm wait guidance and example payloads. bootstrapWave records progress in a ConfigMap so helm --wait behaves deterministically.
Diego Romero: Question on quota creation race: can two concurrent installers create conflicting ResourceQuotas? Add a leader-check or use server-side apply with fieldManager.
Author: Implemented server-side apply semantics in the init job and added a small leader-elect annotation when enforce=true. Documentation updated.

Lina Chen: CI failed initially on templating tests due to missing helper import. Confirmed green after fix. Consider adding a short circuit when cluster has less than X allocatable CPUs to avoid useless waves.
Author: Added short-circuit logic and corresponding unit test; CI now passes.

release_notes: Introduce 'constraintPolicy' (dry-run by default) to declare resource and affinity guardrails; add optional prewarm.sidecar for air-gapped image verification; add 'bootstrapWave' sequencing to stage tenant initialization and upgrades. Operators must opt-in to enforcement. See charts/private-installer/README.md for migration steps.
